solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bow has only one old bus station?

indicators.note: keeping just one of a doubled letter means a duplicate copy must be dropped

blocks.note: to bow is to bend forward, to stoop
O is the standard abbreviation for old; one of the two is removed

explanation.surface: An archer's bow, or a curtsey, oddly linked to an old bus depot.
explanation.walkthrough: STOOP has two Os; letting it keep only one leaves STOP. The question mark flags that a bus stop is a very modest 'station'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus stop is the place where buses halt for passengers, a playful kind of roadside station.

clue.text: Chaps keen to set out computer jargon

indicators.note: to set out is to lay things out afresh, so the letters are arranged in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, all eleven letters

explanation.surface: Men eager to explain the baffling vocabulary of computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder; only 'set out' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Technospeak is the specialised vocabulary of technical people, which is exactly what computer jargon is.

clue.text: Expert movement garnering support

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
motion is movement

explanation.surface: A skilled campaign or political movement winning more backers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests a cause attracting followers, but it is simply a synonym for physical motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion of a cause or product is active backing of it, so the noun matches support as advocacy.

clue.text: Chaotic little dog without lead gets disowned, sadly

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, and going without it means dropping that letter
something gone sadly wrong is out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a pup is a young dog
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild puppy that slipped its leash ends up abandoned by its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a dog's leash, but it means the first letter. 'Gets' simply joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Things turned upside-down are in total disarray, so the hyphenated adjective works as a synonym for chaotic.

clue.text: In Paris, a large centre for teens remains free

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: UN is French for 'a'
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the central letter of the five
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A big Parisian youth centre where the teenagers stay free of rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' tells you to translate the next word into French. 'Remains' looks like a verb but is the noun for ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to release or set loose, so as a verb it matches free in the sense of liberate.

clue.text: Entertainer who might generate a sudden impact? No

indicators.note: to generate is to produce something new, so these letters are made into a fresh word

blocks.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters including the final word

explanation.surface: Is this performer someone who lands a sudden blow? Apparently not.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'No' reads as an answer to the question, yet it supplies the last two letters of the fodder; a stand-up does aim to land punchlines.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up comedian is a solo performer telling jokes on stage, one familiar type of entertainer.

clue.text: Resident properly involved in bloody uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising up means the word is read from bottom to top
being involved in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: doing something properly is doing it well
blood is red

explanation.surface: A local caught up in a violent revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody uprising' reads as a violent rebellion, but 'uprising' only means reading upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is someone who lives in a place, a straightforward synonym for an inhabitant or resident.

clue.text: Love huge end of a series

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
mega is slang for huge

explanation.surface: Adoring the big finale of a TV series.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a television finale; it means the final letter of the Greek alphabet, and by extension the last of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last Greek letter, so it stands for the final item or conclusion of any sequence.

clue.text: Language that is somewhat hidden or secretive

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the following text is used

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A tongue that is partly concealed and mysterious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden or secretive' reads as describing the language, but it is the run of text that holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse, or Old Norse, is the medieval Scandinavian tongue of the Vikings, so it is a language.

clue.text: Third best exam mark secured by horribly loathsome kid in your class?

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast within it
something horribly mangled is badly disordered, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: grades run A, B, C, so the third best is C
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful brat in your form who gets a mediocre C in the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The C sits after the first letter of the rearranged LOATHSOME. The question mark admits a schoolmate need not be in your actual class.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmate is a fellow pupil at the same school, often one taught alongside you in lessons.

clue.text: Shred leaves with front part of rake

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so that alone is used

blocks.note: tea comes as dried leaves
the opening letter of the garden tool

explanation.surface: Tearing up autumn leaves with the tines of a garden rake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like fallen foliage or a verb, but it is tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred something is to rip it into pieces, so the verb tear is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Coat mostly stuffed with good wool

indicators.note: mostly means not entirely, so the final letter is dropped
something stuffed with filling has it packed inside

blocks.note: an anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket; its last letter goes
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A jacket padded out with quality knitting yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: ANORAK without its K becomes ANORA, and G slips in after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is the soft fibre from Angora rabbits or goats, a type of fine wool used in knitting.

clue.text: Deeply, oddly enlightened state

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth

blocks.note: letters one, three and five
an enlightened person is aware

explanation.surface: A curious, profoundly spiritual condition of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enlightened state' reads as nirvana, a state of mind; the state is in fact one of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is one of the fifty United States, the first to ratify the Constitution, so it is a state.

clue.text: One in regiment deployed for horsey event

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
troops deployed are spread out into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: an ace is the one in a suit of cards
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier from a cavalry regiment sent out to a show-jumping event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regiment deployed' suggests troops on manoeuvres, and 'One' a single soldier; the card sense of one is what's needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A race meeting is a day of horse races at a racecourse, so it is very much an equestrian occasion.

clue.text: Way to tuck into excellent drink

indicators.note: to tuck into a meal is to put it inside you, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A method for getting stuck into a superb glass of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a British term for first-rate; setters often turn its digit into the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy, so it is an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Advertiser’s rate for feature during sci-fi show?

blocks.note: a hyper is someone who hypes a product, with the possessive S
pace is rate of movement

explanation.surface: What a TV advertiser charges for a slot in the middle of a science-fiction programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' suggests a fee for airtime, but it means speed. The definition is cryptic: ships in sci-fi shows travel through hyperspace.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperspace is the fictional extra dimension used for faster-than-light travel, a stock element of space-opera films and series.

clue.text: Ruler in crown drinking last drop of Barolo wine

indicators.note: the last drop of something is its final bit, so only the closing letter is kept
drinking takes liquid inside, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: the pate is the crown of the head
the final letter of the Italian wine
tent is a deep red Spanish wine, old-fashioned but crossword-familiar

explanation.surface: A crowned monarch sipping the dregs of a glass of fine Italian red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' suggests royal headgear to suit 'Ruler', but it is the top of the head. O and TENT together go inside after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or sovereign with great power, so the noun is a grand synonym for a ruler.

clue.text: A respectable, short debtor’s note ultimately proves damaging

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter
ultimately means in the end, so just the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: per means a, as in so much per head
nice can mean respectable or proper; its last letter goes
an IOU is a written promise to repay
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A decent but brief note from someone in debt turns out to be harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like the article but stands for PER, as in a pound a day. 'Short' qualifies only NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernicious describes something with a harmful, often gradual and insidious effect, matching damaging as an adjective.

clue.text: Acclaimed cellist initially passed on a track

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter
a runner who passes another a full circuit ahead has lapped them

explanation.surface: A celebrated cellist who first played a piece that was then recorded as an album track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' suggests a recording, natural beside 'cellist', but it is a running track.
explanation.definitionFit: To be clapped is to be applauded by an audience, so the past participle matches acclaimed.

clue.text: Brief problem supported by Queen

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
Mary is the name of several English and Scottish queens

explanation.surface: A short-lived difficulty propped up by royal backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece supported by another sits on top of it. 'Brief' looks like an adjective but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief can be a concise account of the key points, which is exactly what a summary provides.

clue.text: Turn to put out what prisoners do

indicators.note: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to emit is to give out or put out

explanation.surface: An instruction to switch something off, set beside a prison routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like the definition, a spell or go, but it signals the reversal. Prisoners are said to 'do time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing time is the idiom for serving a prison sentence, so the noun is what inmates are said to do.

clue.text: Alarm about family’s use of certain cosmetics?

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a scare is a sudden alarm
kin are relatives, family

explanation.surface: Panic over a household's cosmetics habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after family reads as 'has' or a possessive and is only surface glue; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Skincare is the routine of looking after your complexion, which commonly involves creams, moisturisers and similar products.

clue.text: Stint requiring months in spring

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: to skip is to spring or jump lightly
M is the abbreviation for months

explanation.surface: A work placement that lasts several months during the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stint' looks like a noun, a spell of work, and 'spring' like the season; both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: To stint is to be sparing or mean with something, so as a verb it is a synonym for being frugal or stingy.

clue.text: Stupid way programme ends?

blocks.note: surface reading: the daft manner in which some TV show finishes
setter's reading: describe in words how the spelling of 'programme' finishes, naming its final letter with an article and a preposition

explanation.surface: A sneer at some silly show's daft ending.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'way programme ends' literally: the word 'programme' ends IN AN E. The question mark flags this self-referential trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or lacking sense, which makes it a close synonym for foolish or stupid.

clue.text: Motorway stopped being repaired

blocks.note: M is used for motorways in Britain, as in the M1
stopped means finished, ended

explanation.surface: A motorway closed while roadworks are carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: British motorways are numbered with M, such as the M25 around London.
explanation.definitionFit: Mended means fixed or restored to working order, so the past participle is a synonym for repaired.

clue.text: Religious leader shortly after midnight taking in mass

indicators.note: to take something in is to receive it inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: one o'clock in the morning, 1 a.m., with the numeral read as I
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A cleric arriving soon after twelve at night to celebrate Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service, but it is the scientific symbol. Shortly after midnight is 1 a.m., written I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque and guides a Muslim community, so he is a religious leader.

clue.text: Prudish, naff, fancy idea regularly ignored before closer scrutiny

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals means skipping every other letter, so alternate letters remain

blocks.note: prim means prudish and proper
the second, fourth, sixth and following even letters

explanation.surface: A judgement of some fussy, tacky notion made before looking at it properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky. 'Fancy' looks like an anagram signal but is just fodder for the alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Prima facie is Latin for 'at first sight', describing how something appears on initial impression without deeper examination.

clue.text: Leader’s position in group’s last run of gigs

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the closing letter of the word before the possessive
a residency is a series of shows by a band at one venue

explanation.surface: A frontman's place in the band during their final tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' and 'group' suggest a rock band; the leader is a head of state or of an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The presidency is the office held by a president, so it is the role or post of a leader.

clue.text: As a result, work unit introduces nothing

blocks.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Consequently, a team at the office brings in zero output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work unit' suggests a department or team; here it is the scientific unit of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to mean consequently, so it introduces a conclusion.
